stemBlocks.value: Make P the subject of the formula M = √(P + 2M).
Think first: M appears on both sides, but only P has to be isolated, so treat M as an ordinary letter throughout.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p096-q14 from workbook page 96.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Square both sides to remove the root, then subtract 2M.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: P = M² − 2M, which may also be written P = M(M − 2)

whyThisWorks.value: The square root already stands alone, so squaring immediately removes it and turns the formula into a simple linear equation in P. The fact that M appears twice does not matter here, because M is not the subject — every M can be left exactly where it lands.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing M² = P + 2M², squaring the terms inside the root separately.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing M² = P + 2M², squaring the terms inside the root separately.

commonErrors.misconception: Trying to cancel M across the equation.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Trying to cancel M across the equation.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing P = M² + 2M with the wrong sign.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing P = M² + 2M with the wrong sign.

examTip.value: Squaring a root removes the whole bracket underneath it at once — never square the terms inside individually.
